;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Korean conflict]]
**[[Korean People's Army Ground Force|North]] and [[Republic of Korea Army|South Korean soldiers]] exchange gunfire across the [[Korean Demilitarized Zone|DMZ]] at a [[South Korea]]n guard post in [[Cheorwon County|Cheorwon]], but no injuries are reported. South Korean and U.S. officials suspect the initial shots from the north to be accidental. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-52518844 (BBC News)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-northkorea-southorea/north-and-south-korea-exchange-gunfire-across-border-at-guard-post-idUSKBN22F03N?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Piracy in the Gulf of Guinea]]
**Unidentified forces attack two fishing vessels near the Gabonese capital of [[Libreville]] and abduct six crewmen (3 Indonesian, 2 Senegalese, and a South Korean). It is the second pirate attack reported this year off the coast of [[Gabon]]. [http://www.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20200506000706 (''The Korea Herald'')]
*[[Sinai insurgency]]
**[[Egypt]]'s [[Egyptian Armed Forces|military]] says that 15 of its members were killed or wounded in recent operations in [[Sinai Peninsula|Sinai]] and that 126 suspected militants had been killed. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-egypt-security/egypt-reports-15-military-casualties-in-sinai-recently-idUSKBN22F0L7?il=0 (Reuters)]
*[[Macuto Bay raid]], [[Crisis in Venezuela]]
**Former [[United States Army Special Forces#The Green Beret|U.S. Green Beret]] [[Jordan Goudreau]], who took part in the failed [[2019 Venezuelan uprising attempt]] to oust [[Nicolás Maduro]], releases a video claiming responsibility for an incursion in Venezuela, announcing the start of an effort to capture senior Venezuelan officials wanted by the U.S. government, codenamed [[Macuto Bay raid|"Operation Gideon"]]. Goudreau claims 60 troops have successfully entered Venezuela by "land and sea" and fighting is underway. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/the_americas/venezuela-maduro-armed-invasion-guaido-opposition/2020/05/03/efb2fa88-8d51-11ea-9322-a29e75effc93_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
**[[Venezuela]]n Interior Minister [[Néstor Reverol]] says the country's security forces have foiled a "marine incursion" by "[[Terrorism|terrorist]] [[Mercenary|mercenaries]]" from [[Colombia]], killing at least eight gunmen and capturing two others. The foreign group reportedly landed on a beach in the city of [[La Guaira]] on [[speedboat]]s. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2020/05/venezuela-killed-foiled-invasion-sea-200503162349161.html (Al Jazeera)]
**[[State media|State television]] broadcasts images it says are captured high-calibre weapons, [[Peru]]vian documents, and uniforms emblazoned with an [[Flag of the United States|American flag]]. [https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/6743950/boat-attack-on-venezuela-port-foiled/?cs=14264 (''Canberra Times'')]

;Business and economy
*[[Indonesia]]n [[e-commerce]] site [[Tokopedia]] launches a security investigation after a [[hacker]] said they stole the information of 91 million users and plans to release it on the [[dark web]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-tokopedia-cyber/indonesias-tokopedia-probes-alleged-data-leak-of-91-million-users-idUSKBN22E0Q2?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
***[[Russia]] reports a record 10,633 new cases of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]] and 58 more deaths from the virus in the last 24 hours, bringing the country's total cases to 134,686 and 1,280 deaths. [[Moscow]]'s [[mayor of Moscow|mayor]] [[Sergei Sobyanin]] says the peak has still not been reached, warning residents to remain indoors. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-europe-52521426 (BBC News)]
